rule.name: SeImpersonatePrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies whether SeImpersonatePrivilege is present and whether it is enabled. Presence is evidence, not proof of a usable impersonation path.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Privilege is enabled
A trusted privileged authentication flow is reachable

rule.limitations: Does not trigger or exploit an authentication flow.
rule.recommendation: Enumerate reachable local services and token sources, then validate platform mitigations.

rule.name: SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies assignment-primary-token capability while preserving the distinction between present and enabled.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Required companion privileges and a suitable token are available

rule.limitations: No token is created or assigned.
rule.recommendation: Verify companion privileges, target token provenance, and process-creation restrictions.

rule.name: SeBackupPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies backup semantics that may bypass parts of normal file access checking when explicitly used.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Privilege is enabled for a backup-semantics operation

rule.limitations: Does not prove access to a protected file and reads no secrets.
rule.recommendation: Validate access against an authorized non-sensitive test object using backup semantics.

rule.name: SeRestorePrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies restore semantics relevant to privileged writes and ownership operations.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Privilege is enabled for a restore-semantics operation

rule.limitations: Performs no write, restore, ownership, or ACL operation.
rule.recommendation: Review authorized targets and the exact restore API semantics required.

rule.name: SeDebugPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies debug privilege while noting protected processes and other platform restrictions.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Target process is not protected against the caller

rule.limitations: Does not open or inspect another process.
rule.recommendation: Inventory only authorized target protections and validate access non-destructively.

rule.name: SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies the ability to become owner of securable objects, subject to object type and policy.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: A relevant securable target exists

rule.limitations: Does not change ownership or permissions.
rule.recommendation: Review authorized object types and distinguish ownership from effective write access.

rule.name: SeLoadDriverPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies driver-load privilege; signing, code integrity, policy, and OS version remain material constraints.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Code integrity and driver policy permit the candidate

rule.limitations: Loads no driver and does not assess vulnerable drivers.
rule.recommendation: Review code-integrity policy and approved driver inventory.

rule.name: SeManageVolumePrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies volume-management privilege without treating it as direct escalation.

required.condition: Privilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: A relevant volume operation and target are available

rule.limitations: Performs no volume operation.
rule.recommendation: Review authorized volume-management capabilities and OS-specific controls.

rule.name: Server Operators

evidence.item: Token group SID and enabled or deny-only attributes

rule.description: Uses the well-known SID to identify effective Server Operators membership.

required.condition: S-1-5-32-549 is enabled and not deny-only

optional.condition: A privileged service or server object is controllable

invalidating.condition: Membership is absent, disabled, or deny-only

rule.limitations: Effective capabilities vary with server role and object ACLs.
rule.recommendation: Correlate membership with enumerated service rights and token privileges.

rule.name: Backup Operators

evidence.item: Token group SID and enabled or deny-only attributes

rule.description: Uses the well-known SID to identify effective Backup Operators membership.

required.condition: S-1-5-32-551 is enabled and not deny-only

optional.condition: Backup or restore privileges are present

invalidating.condition: Membership is absent, disabled, or deny-only

rule.limitations: Membership alone does not prove protected-resource access.
rule.recommendation: Correlate with SeBackupPrivilege, SeRestorePrivilege, and authorized targets.

rule.name: DnsAdmins

evidence.item: Scoped token group SID, resolved account, and group attributes

rule.description: Identifies a token group resolving to DnsAdmins; this group has no universal fixed SID.

required.condition: An enabled non-deny-only token SID resolves to the scoped DnsAdmins account

optional.condition: The DNS Server role and relevant service rights are present

invalidating.condition: Membership is absent, disabled, or deny-only

rule.limitations: Name resolution is localization and domain-scope sensitive; service control is evaluated separately.
rule.recommendation: Confirm the group SID in the intended domain and correlate it with DNS service configuration rights.

rule.name: Print Operators

evidence.item: Token group SID and enabled or deny-only attributes

rule.description: Uses the well-known SID to identify effective Print Operators membership.

required.condition: S-1-5-32-550 is enabled and not deny-only

optional.condition: Version-specific printer or driver capability remains available

invalidating.condition: Membership is absent, disabled, or deny-only

rule.limitations: Capabilities vary across Windows versions and hardened configurations.
rule.recommendation: Verify print subsystem state, policy, and token privileges for the specific host.

rule.name: Writable Service Binary

evidence.item: Service executable path, AccessCheck result, and service account

rule.description: Correlates effective write access to the exact service executable with a higher-privilege service identity.

required.condition: Exact service executable is writable
Service account is privileged

optional.condition: Service start conditions are reachable

rule.limitations: Does not replace a binary or start a service.
rule.recommendation: Review the exact executable ACL, service identity, start behavior, and file protection controls.

rule.name: Weak Service Configuration Permissions

evidence.item: OpenService access result and service account

rule.description: Tests whether SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG can be opened for the current token and correlates the service identity.

required.condition: SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG is effectively granted
Service account is privileged

optional.condition: Service can be started by an authorized mechanism

rule.limitations: Does not modify service configuration.
rule.recommendation: Review the service DACL and remove unnecessary SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG grants.

rule.name: Unquoted Service Path

evidence.item: Raw command line, candidate paths, AccessCheck results, and service account

rule.description: Requires an unquoted executable path with spaces, a concrete search candidate, a controllable directory, and a privileged service identity.

required.condition: Service path is unquoted and contains spaces
A concrete candidate location is controllable
Service account is privileged

optional.condition: Candidate does not already block creation

invalidating.condition: Path is quoted or no candidate location is controllable

rule.limitations: Conservative directory correlation can return UNKNOWN; it never creates a candidate.
rule.recommendation: Quote the executable path and restrict create/write rights on every candidate directory.

rule.name: Writable Service Executable Directory

evidence.item: Executable directory AccessCheck result and service account

rule.description: Correlates directory file-creation rights around a service executable with a higher-privilege service identity.

required.condition: Executable directory permits relevant creation
Service account is privileged

optional.condition: A concrete loading or replacement relationship exists

rule.limitations: Directory creation is not equivalent to replacing the existing executable.
rule.recommendation: Review the concrete load path and restrict create, delete, rename, and ACL rights as applicable.

rule.name: Writable Scheduled Task Binary

evidence.item: Registered task, enabled state, exact action, target AccessCheck, and principal

rule.description: Correlates an enabled registered task, its exact executable, effective write access, and a higher execution principal.

required.condition: Enabled task has an Exec action referencing the exact executable
Executable is effectively writable
Principal is higher privileged

optional.condition: An active trigger exists

invalidating.condition: No registered task references the executable or AccessCheck denies write

rule.limitations: Does not run the task or modify the executable.
rule.recommendation: Review the task action, triggers, principal, run level, and target ACL.

rule.name: Weak Scheduled Task Permissions

evidence.item: Registered task security descriptor AccessCheck and principal

rule.description: Evaluates the task security descriptor for a relevant modification right and correlates a higher execution principal.

required.condition: Task definition is modifiable
Principal is higher privileged

optional.condition: Task registration service accepts the operation

rule.limitations: Task Scheduler may apply additional registration checks beyond the DACL.
rule.recommendation: Review the registered task security descriptor and registration policy.

rule.name: Writable Scheduled Task Script

evidence.item: Registered task action, script type, target AccessCheck, and principal

rule.description: Correlates an enabled task action referencing a script, effective script write access, and a higher principal.

required.condition: Enabled task references the exact script
Script is effectively writable
Principal is higher privileged

optional.condition: Interpreter and arguments resolve as expected

invalidating.condition: Target is not a script or write is denied

rule.limitations: Does not edit or execute the script.
rule.recommendation: Restrict script modification and review interpreter arguments and task principal.

rule.name: Scheduled Task Execution Path Hijacking

evidence.item: Task path form, resolution target permission, working directory, and principal

rule.description: Requires a relative or ambiguous task execution path, a concrete controllable target, and a higher principal.

required.condition: Task execution path is relative or ambiguous
A concrete resolution target is controllable
Principal is higher privileged

optional.condition: Working directory and process environment preserve the resolution order

invalidating.condition: Execution path is absolute and unambiguous or no target is controllable

rule.limitations: Runtime environment and application-specific loading behavior may differ.
rule.recommendation: Use absolute quoted paths and restrict every concrete search location.

rule.name: AlwaysInstallElevated

evidence.item: Both machine and current-user AlwaysInstallElevated policy values

rule.description: Detects the Windows Installer policy only when both the machine and current-user values are enabled, as required by Microsoft.

required.condition: HKLM AlwaysInstallElevated equals 1
HKCU AlwaysInstallElevated equals 1

optional.condition: Windows Installer is available and application-control policy permits the package

invalidating.condition: Either policy value is absent or not equal to 1

rule.limitations: Does not generate, install, or execute an MSI package. Application control and installer policy can impose further restrictions.
rule.recommendation: Disable the policy in both Computer and User Configuration and review MSI execution from user-writable paths.

rule.name: Event Log Readers

evidence.item: Enabled non-deny-only membership in SID S-1-5-32-573

rule.description: Identifies effective Event Log Readers membership. This is an information-access capability, not direct privilege escalation.

required.condition: S-1-5-32-573 is enabled and not deny-only

optional.condition: Readable logs contain sensitive command-line or script content
Process command-line auditing is enabled

invalidating.condition: Membership is absent, disabled, or deny-only

rule.limitations: Does not read event contents or collect credentials. Event 4688 command lines are empty unless the relevant audit policy is enabled.
rule.recommendation: Review membership, audit-log ACLs, and whether commands or scripts expose secrets in logs.

rule.name: SeTcbPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies the Act as part of the operating system privilege while leaving token-construction and authentication-package conditions unproven.

required.condition: SeTcbPrivilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Privilege is enabled
A compatible token or authentication operation is available

rule.limitations: Does not create tokens, log on users, register authentication packages, or perform S4U operations.
rule.recommendation: Remove this right from non-TCB accounts and investigate why it is present.

rule.name: Print Spooler Impersonation Surface

evidence.item: Running Spooler service identity plus enabled SeImpersonatePrivilege

rule.description: Correlates a running privileged Print Spooler with enabled SeImpersonatePrivilege. It identifies an authentication surface, not a guaranteed exploit.

required.condition: Spooler service is running
Spooler runs as a privileged identity
SeImpersonatePrivilege is present and enabled

optional.condition: Host version, patches, RPC behavior, and named-pipe conditions permit a documented technique

invalidating.condition: Spooler is stopped or disabled, or SeImpersonatePrivilege is unavailable

rule.limitations: Does not coerce authentication, create a named pipe, or test PrintSpoofer/SpoolSample. Modern mitigations can rule out specific techniques.
rule.recommendation: Disable Spooler where unnecessary, especially on domain controllers and identity infrastructure, and validate patch and RPC exposure.

reference.title: Disable Print spooler service on domain controllers
reference.author: Microsoft

rule.name: SeCreateTokenPrivilege

evidence.item: Token privilege name, presence, and enabled state

rule.description: Identifies the Create a token object privilege in the current token. Microsoft documents that it is required to create a primary token and warns that assigning it outside LocalSystem can allow complete control of the system.

required.condition: SeCreateTokenPrivilege is present in the current token

optional.condition: Privilege is enabled
A compatible token-creation operation and required inputs are available

rule.limitations: Does not create, modify, duplicate, assign, or impersonate a token. Presence alone does not prove that a usable privileged token was created.
rule.recommendation: Do not assign Create a token object to users or services other than LocalSystem unless a documented operating-system requirement exists; investigate any unexpected assignment.

rule.name: Weak Service Registry Configuration Permissions

evidence.item: Targeted service registry key, view, owner, DACL ACEs, and effective KEY_SET_VALUE/KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY/DELETE/WRITE_DAC result

rule.description: Correlates a service already enumerated through SCM with effective mutation rights on its own registry configuration and a higher service identity. Registry-key rights are kept distinct from SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG on the SCM object.

required.condition: The service was enumerated through SCM
The service runs as a higher identity
AccessCheck grants a concrete registry mutation right on the service or relevant Parameters key

optional.condition: The current user can start or restart the service
A specific ImagePath or ServiceDll value is present

invalidating.condition: The service identity is not higher or the effective token is denied all relevant mutation rights

rule.limitations: Collection is read-only and restricted to keys of SCM-enumerated services. KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY without a concrete writable value is POTENTIAL, not CONFIRMED. SACL and mandatory-label effects remain UNKNOWN when unavailable.
rule.recommendation: Remove low-privilege KEY_SET_VALUE, KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY, DELETE, WRITE_DAC, and ownership rights from service configuration keys and their Parameters subkeys.

reference.title: Registry Key Security and Access Rights
reference.author: Microsoft

reference.title: HKLM System CurrentControlSet Services Registry Tree
reference.author: Microsoft

rule.name: Writable Privileged ServiceDll

evidence.item: Privileged shared-process service, configured ServiceDll path, path existence, effective file/directory rights, and explicit CONFIGURED relationship

rule.description: Correlates a shared-process service running as a higher identity with its configured ServiceDll and effective replacement rights. The rule records configuration only; it does not infer that the DLL is loaded.

required.condition: A shared-process service has a ServiceDll registry value
The service runs as a higher identity
The existing DLL is effectively writable

optional.condition: The service host process is currently observed by exact PID
A missing DLL can be created in its parent directory

invalidating.condition: No ServiceDll is configured, the service is not shared-process/higher-identity, or effective replacement rights are denied

rule.limitations: CONFIRMED means the detection preconditions were verified, not that loading or code execution occurred. Missing DLL or indirect ACL-control cases remain POTENTIAL; inaccessible evidence is UNKNOWN.
rule.recommendation: Protect the configured DLL and parent directory, correct the service-key DACL, and validate the service configuration through approved change control.
